plan.topic: Is retatrutide approved yet? A dated status check for the US, UK, Canada and Australia (Oct 2026)
plan.angle: First line: 'Is retatrutide approved yet? Not yet. As of Oct 2026 it isn't approved by the FDA, the UK's MHRA, Health Canada or Australia's TGA.' Then: 'Lilly reported Phase 3 results in July 2026 and says it plans to submit to the FDA in early 2027. A plan to file isn't approval.' One number: 'In TRIUMPH-2, published in The Lancet, adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight lost 20.8% on the top dose vs 4.0% on placebo over 80 weeks.' Then: 'CBS News reported the FDA received at least two death reports after people used products sold as retatrutide. Reports don't show the product caused the deaths, but the FDA warns these products aren't the trial drug.' One GI line, the prescriber or clinical-trial route, 'follow for more' and the prescriber line.
plan.why: Spin-off of L1. Retatrutide is our strongest Shorts lane (182/98/63), the dated status question is our best Instagram format (patch, 85 reach), and death-report coverage is pushing status searches up. Slot it at 08:00 or 13:00. | fact-check: Matches our best Instagram format (a dated status question) and the retatrutide lane. Checked: Lilly announced TRIUMPH-2/-3 results in Jul 2026 and plans an FDA submission in Q1 2027. CBS News reported FDA documents showing at least two death reports this year tied to illicit products sold as retatrutide, not linked to Lilly's trials (Gizmodo, Newsweek and others citing CBS). Fixes: (a) the placebo figure conflicts between sources: the Lancet paper says 4.0%, Lilly's topline says 3.2%. Use the Lancet figure, credit it to the paper and keep the estimand consistent with L1; (b) say 'at least two' death reports, credited to CBS News reporting on FDA documents, and keep 'a report doesn't show the product caused the death'; (c) write 'Lilly says it plans to submit', not 'will file'. The death-report line must stay calm, not fear-bait: put it after the status answer, not as the opener. No vials, sellers, doses or sourcing.

package.title: Retatrutide approved yet? (Oct 2026) #shorts
package.description:
Is retatrutide approved yet? Not yet. As of Oct 2026, it isn't approved by the FDA, MHRA, Health Canada or TGA. Lilly says it plans to submit to the FDA in Q1 2027; a plan to file isn't approval. In Lilly's Phase 3 TRIUMPH-2 trial (adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight), the most common side effects were gastrointestinal, like nausea.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
Bellido V, et al. TRIUMPH-2, The Lancet, online first Sep 29, 2026 — https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01861-1
Eli Lilly and Company (PR Newswire), Sep 29, 2026 — https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lillys-triple-agonist-retatrutide-delivered-substantial-weight-loss-and-a1c-reduction-underscoring-its-potential-promise-for-people-with-obesity-and-type-2-diabetes-302891798.html
CBS News, Oct 13, 2026 — https://www.cbsnews.com/news/deaths-reported-fda-bootleg-reta-weight-loss-drug/
U.S. FDA, content current as of Oct 1, 2026 — https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fdas-concerns-unapproved-glp-1-drugs-used-weight-loss

social.instagram_caption:
Retatrutide approved yet? Not yet — as of Oct 2026, it's not approved by the FDA, MHRA, Health Canada or TGA.

Lilly says it plans to file with the FDA in Q1 2027. A plan to file isn't approval.

In Lilly's Phase 3 TRIUMPH-2 trial (adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight), those who stayed on the top dose lost 20.8% of body weight over 80 weeks vs 4.0% on placebo. Counting everyone, it was 18.8% vs 5.1%.

CBS News reported FDA documents show two death reports after people used products sold as retatrutide. A report doesn't prove cause. Lilly said neither was connected to a clinical trial, and Lilly says black-market products have contained the wrong amount or the wrong ingredient. The FDA says retatrutide hasn't been found safe and effective for any condition.

Most common trial side effects: gastrointestinal, like nausea.

Save this so you have the dated facts before you see another "Reta" post.

script.hook_pattern: A dated status question, answered straight away ("Is retatrutide approved yet? Not yet."). Next comes the check with four regulators, then Lilly's plan to submit to the FDA in the first quarter of 2027. Then one TRIUMPH-2 result, credited to The Lancet paper, with both estimands. The 'if stayed on treatment' figure carries its qualifier on screen, and the 'counting everyone' main result follows. The death reports come next, told calmly and credited to CBS News, FDA documents and Lilly. The card says they followed products sold as retatrutide. The FDA's exact wording and Lilly's black-market wording follow. Then one gastrointestinal side-effect line and the prescriber or clinical-trial route. It ends on 'Follow for more', which loops back into the opening question.

factcheck.summary: I checked the claims against primary and secondary sources, and they hold up. Lilly's July 23, 2026 press release says it "plans to submit a Biologics License Application (BLA) for retatrutide to FDA in Q1 2027", which supports the "not approved anywhere yet" status. Lilly's Sep 29 press release and Healio confirm TRIUMPH-2 in The Lancet (Bellido et al.). It enrolled 1,152 adults with type 2 diabetes and BMI ≥27, ran 80 weeks, and gave 12 mg vs placebo: 20.8% vs 4.0% under the efficacy estimand, and 18.8% vs 5.1% under the treatment-regimen estimand. Gastrointestinal effects were the most common adverse events. CBS News (Oct 13, 2026) confirms: two death reports to FDA's adverse event reporting system (FAERS), obtained through a FOIA request; "aren't connected to a formal clinical trial, according to the documents and Eli Lilly"; "the reports alone don't prove" cause; and Lilly found suspect versions "with too much, too little, or the wrong active ingredient". The FDA page (current as of 10/01/2026) says retatrutide has "not been found safe and effective for any condition." Narration is exactly 170 words, which is within the limit. The tone is calm and attributed, it points to a prescriber, and it names no sellers or sources. There are only minor fixes: on-screen scope on s4, an ambiguous "it" in the prescriber line, and the DOI link redirecting.

issues.problem: Muted-viewer test: the caption drops the drug and dose (retatrutide 12 mg), the comparator label (placebo), the 80-week timeframe and 'obesity or overweight', all of which the narration gives. The stat_label has them, but the caption card is weaker than the narration.
issues.fix: Retatrutide 12 mg vs placebo, 80 weeks, if stayed on treatment: 20.8% vs 4.0% (type 2 diabetes + obesity/overweight)

issues.problem: The arm and comparator aren't next to the numbers on screen.
issues.fix: Counting everyone: retatrutide 12 mg 18.8% vs placebo 5.1%

issues.claim: Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.
issues.problem: Coming straight after a section on an unapproved drug, 'it' could be heard as retatrutide, which no prescriber can prescribe outside a trial. Make clear the referent is approved options or a trial. Keep the mandatory line word for word.
issues.fix: Options today: approved medicines or a clinical trial. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you. Follow for more.

issues.claim: Most common trial side effects: gastrointestinal, like nausea.
issues.problem: This is accurate. But in TRIUMPH-2 at 12 mg, diarrhea (33.6%) was more common than nausea (28.0%), according to Lilly's Sep 29 release. It's optional to name both. Note the word count is at 170, so trim elsewhere if you add a word.
issues.fix: Most common trial side effects: gastrointestinal, like diarrhea and nausea. (To stay at 170 words or fewer, change s3 to 'Lilly plans to submit to the FDA in early 2027.' No: keep 'first quarter of 2027' and instead cut 'paper' from s4.)

issues.problem: The DOI redirects (302) and the Lancet page is paywalled (403). Healio and Lilly's Sep 29 release confirm it, so the paywall is acceptable. Our source rule prefers the canonical page URL.
issues.fix: Use https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01861-1/fulltext and keep src6a/src6b as confirming sources.

audio.soundNotes: Music is already in the target window (−13.5 dB under voice) so left at 1.0×; no reason to turn it down further since ducking handles speech-heavy sections. Thinned several 5–7-hit clusters (t≈3–4.8s, 11.8–13.8s, 16.7–17.6s, 51–52s, 69.9–70.5s, 75.6–79.8s) down to 2–4 sounds and removed exact-duplicate simultaneous pairs (e.g., swoosh+whoosh, swoosh+whip at the same timestamp) to avoid stacking. Dropped/attenuated an over-loud blip at 3.81s that was poking above the voice (−5.2 dB). Boosted the two numeric stat reveals (20.8%/4.0% at 30.8s and 18.8%/5.1% at 37.5s) toward the −6 to −12 dB "big reveal" window since they land in natural emphasis points. The FDA "not found safe or effective" cue at 57.5s was essentially inaudible (−37.8 dB) despite being the episode's key regulatory beat, so pushed its gain to the cap and added a custom low thud for weight; also added a light news-chime for the CBS cue and a subtle stomach-gurgle under the GI side-effect label to give that body-mood beat texture without competing with narration.
